deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivation, and it is not by Riemann. It is the second page (86v) of a letter by Richard Dedekind, signed on the next page 'Harzburg, 22 August 1891 (Haus Dedekind)'. Riemann's papers were later filed with it in the 'Waermeleitung' bundle. The addressee is almost certainly Heinrich Weber, who was then preparing the second edition of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1892).

What the letter says:
- The previous page explains that after mailing Weber his package on 'Riemann's Hypothesen der Geometrie', Dedekind remembered his long and largely fruitless correspondence with a professor in Plauen i. V. (read below as Richard Beez). This correspondence concerned Riemann's note for the Paris prize question, the 1861 Commentatio mathematica on heat conduction, and Beez had raised objections to it.
- On this page Dedekind says he recopied his own draft letters, which were nearly illegible from corrections and rearrangements. He is sending the whole exchange as fifteen sheets arranged historically in red ink.
- He thinks some of it is 'really quite good'. He is not sure that what he wrote on sheet 9 about the theory of linear partial differential equations is fully correct, since he has not thought about it for years, but he believes it is.
- Weber may keep the papers as long as he likes. Dedekind wants them back not in Harzburg but later, in October, in Braunschweig.
- He does not have with him Beez's relevant papers printed in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift (für Mathematik und Physik), but suggests Weber look them up.
- He mentions that Felix Klein and his wife visited Harzburg a few days earlier.

The mathematical background is only alluded to, not worked out. Riemann's 1861 Paris memoir asks when a quadratic differential form sum b_ij dx_i dx_j can be transformed into a constant-coefficient form. It introduces the four-index curvature quantities (the Riemann tensor) and states that their vanishing is the criterion. Beez's 1875–1879 papers in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift dealt with the curvature of higher-dimensional manifolds; there he raised objections to the Commentatio, which Dedekind tried to answer. Nothing is derived on this page.

results.what: Historical and archival information only. Dedekind (1891) forwards to Weber his recopied correspondence with Richard Beez about objections to Riemann's 1861 Paris prize memoir (Commentatio mathematica). He mentions his own remarks on linear PDE theory (sheet 9 of that correspondence) and Beez's papers in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift.
results.modern_name: Editorial history of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke, 2nd ed. (1892); reception of the Commentatio and the Riemann curvature tensor
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Commentatio 1861, publ. 1876); Beez (Zeitschr. f. Math. u. Phys., 1875–79); Dedekind–Weber editorial correspondence

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a Dedekind letter of 1891 with no mathematics, only editorial and correspondence details. The Dedekind–Weber collaboration on Riemann's Werke and Beez's discussion of the Commentatio are documented in the literature. The letter is mildly interesting archivally, as evidence of an unpublished Dedekind–Beez exchange, but it contains no result attributable to Riemann.
transcription_corrections: On the previous page, 'Prof. R. Lanz[?] in Plauen i. V.' should almost certainly read 'Prof. R. Beez in Plauen i. V.' (Richard Beez, Gymnasium Plauen). This matches 'Arbeiten von Beez' in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift on this page.
On this page, 'Arbeiten von Beez[?]' is confirmed as 'Beez'.
'rother' is underlined in the manuscript ('mit rother Dinte').
'Harzburg[?]' is confirmed as 'Harzburg' by the signature line on the next page.
On the next page, 'verzögert[?]' is probably 'verweilt' or similar (uncertain).
The page is by Dedekind, not Riemann; the attribution of folio 86v in the bundle to Riemann's hand is misleading.
